simple.meaning: אֲגַם (ʼăgam) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a marsh ; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Exodus, Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Exodus 7:19. Its contexts include blood, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲגַם (H98).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: a marsh ; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds
definitions.full: H98. agam אֲגַם noun [masculine] troubled pool (Aramaic id. , , Assyrian agammu Dl W ) — ׳א absolute Isa 35:7 ; construct 41:18 2 t.; אֲגַמִּים Exod 8:1-2 t.; אַגְמֵי Isa 14:23 ; אַגְמֵיהֶם Exod 7:19 — 1 troubled or muddy (gloomy) pools or marshes , plural ׳א מַיִם Isa 14:23 . 2 any pool, pond , singular ׳א מַיִם Isa 41:18 ; Psa 107:35 ; 114:8 ; plural without מַיִם Exod 7:19 ; 8:1 (P) Isa 42:15 . 3 swamp-reed, rush (= אַגְמוֺן ) Jer 51:32 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root (meaning to collect as water);

There will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and in vessels of stone.’ ”
